title: The 24-hour margin call cure period is only safe because the Liquidation LTV overrides it
content:
A.6.1.1.1.3.8.2.4.2.3 grants a generous window: "the maximum permitted margin call cure period is **24 hours** from the time the Maintenance LTV is breached." In crypto markets, 24 hours is long enough for a collateral asset to halve.

What makes the grace tolerable is the clause in the Liquidation LTV definition (A.6.1.1.1.3.8.2.2.1.3): liquidation is permitted "**regardless of whether there is an outstanding margin call in effect**."

So the cure period is a concession about *time*, not about *price*. A borrower whose position drifted from 85% to 86% gets a day to wire collateral — which is a real accommodation for an institutional counterparty operating in business hours, across banking systems, with humans in the loop. A borrower whose collateral gaps from 85% to 91% gets nothing; the cure clock is irrelevant because the price condition has already been met.

Without the override, the two provisions would combine into a disaster: a 24-hour contractual immunity beginning at exactly the moment a position starts failing, during which no liquidation could occur no matter how far the collateral fell. Every borrower would have an incentive to trip the maintenance level deliberately in a falling market to buy a day of protection.

The pairing is what makes the numbers legible. The maintenance-to-liquidation gap — 5 points for BTC and ETH, 10 for XRP and HYPE — is the price buffer the grace period is allowed to consume. The cure period is not really 24 hours; it is 24 hours *or* five points of collateral value, whichever runs out first, and for volatile assets the second is usually the binding one.
description: Liquidation may occur immediately above the Liquidation LTV 'regardless of whether there is an outstanding margin call', so the grace period yields on price but never on a collapsing position.
